items.title: Should Plymouth join the Devon and Torbay Combined County Authority (and seek an elected mayor)?
items.body: Plymouth City Council, Devon County Council, Torbay Council and the Devon and Torbay Combined County Authority
items.time: Consultation closed 28 October 2026. Decisions: Plymouth City Council 23 November, the Authority board 25 November, Devon County Council 3 December, Torbay Council 10 December 2026 (per The Exeter Times, 17 November).
items.plain: Closed on 28 October. Most people who answered backed Plymouth joining and a mayor. Plymouth City Council votes on 23 November, then the Authority, Devon and Torbay decide by 10 December. If all agree, it goes to the Government.
items.detail: Plymouth City Council's news item (16 September 2026) says a six-week consultation ran to 28 October 2026 on Plymouth becoming a full member, and that the Authority would seek mayoral status; a mayor would not run local councils, and bin collections, schools, social care, housing and planning would stay with councils. The Combined County Authority's news page (28 October 2026, read 2 November) says the Budget confirmed the Government is minded to proceed with a Mayoral Strategic Authority for Devon, Plymouth and Torbay; responses are being analysed and findings will be published before decisions; each council and the Authority will take formal decisions between November and December 2026; if all agree and Parliament approves, the authority could start in autumn 2027 with the first mayoral election expected in May 2028. Update 16 November 2026: The Herald (10 November, Local Democracy Reporter) says final edits were being made to Plymouth's proposal to join the Authority and the papers would be published that Friday following the consultation; the council leader said a mayoral authority could bring a 30-year investment fund of around £750 million. The Moorlander (9 November) says the first mayor is expected to take office in spring 2028. The Plymouth democracy feed (home-computer scrape, 16 November) shows a City Council agenda published for Monday 23 November 2026 at 2pm; I could not read whether this item is on it. Update 23 November 2026: The Herald (18 November, Local Democracy Reporter, read in full) says 352 survey responses (157 from Plymouth) and 23 stakeholder responses were received; across Devon 60 per cent agreed with Plymouth joining and 63 per cent with a mayoral model, in Plymouth 54 and 58 per cent, and in Torbay opinion was evenly split. Councillors are recommended to give consent on Monday 23 November. The Exeter Times (17 November, read in full) says the decision order is Plymouth (23 November), the Authority board (25 November), Devon County Council (3 December) and Torbay Council (10 December), aiming to submit before the end of 2026 so the Government can make regulations in early 2027; the proposed 13-member board gives Exeter and two district councils seats without guaranteed votes, and South Hams and West Devon councils said they would not support a mayoral authority unless district councils get full voting rights. The outcome of the 23 November meeting was not known when this was collected.
items.how: The consultation has closed. Watch the Plymouth City Council decision (23 November), the Authority board (25 November), Devon County Council (3 December) and Torbay Council (10 December).

items.title: Local government reorganisation: Greater Plymouth plan (13 South Hams parishes) withdrawn for review
items.body: UK Government (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)
items.time: Government consultation closed 26 March 2026. Proposal withdrawn for a further review on 29 October 2026. The Herald (10 November) says news is due within two months; district councils expect to hear in March 2027 (neither is a Government date).
items.plain: The Government's plan to enlarge Plymouth by 13 South Hams parishes, including Ivybridge, was approved in July, paused in September and withdrawn for a further review on 29 October. A fresh decision is due in 2027.
items.detail: The Herald (29 October 2026, read in full) reports the Government has withdrawn its favoured proposal for Devon, which included a Greater Plymouth Council taking in 13 South Hams parishes, and will put it through a further review with a fresh decision in 2027. Plymouth City Council's leader said the council was disappointed and will make its case again when the review begins; the Government still aims for shadow authority elections in 2028 and new councils in 2029. A local MP's social post (search snippet only) also says ministers have formally withdrawn the plan. Earlier history: the Government consultation closed at 11.59pm on 26 March 2026 (gov.uk); the plan was approved in July 2026 and paused in September 2026. No review timetable has been published yet. Devon Air Radio (Local Democracy Reporter, 5 November 2026, read 9 November) reports that Devon's district councils expect to hear in March 2027 what happens next; this is a council expectation, not a Government date. Update 16 November 2026: The Herald (10 November) reports news on reorganisation for Devon is due in the next two months and that the plan may come back, be scrapped or be replaced; Hits Radio (16 November) confirms Devon is among nine areas whose decisions were withdrawn for review.
items.how: No open consultation. Watch for the Government's review and the councils' statements; contact your MP or parish councillor.

items.title: Hemerdon Mine: permit change for the mineral processing plant (Drakelands Restoration Ltd)
items.time: Comments by 11 December 2026 (closing time not stated)
items.plain: The Environment Agency is asking for comments on a big change to the environmental permit for the processing plant at Hemerdon tungsten mine, between Plympton and Dartmoor. The permit sets limits on emissions such as noise, dust and water.
items.detail: From the Environment Agency notice on GOV.UK (published 13 November 2026): Drakelands Restoration Limited has applied to vary its permit (EPR/AP3203ML/V003) with a substantial change, for a mineral processing facility at Hemerdon Mine, Drakelands, Plympton PL7 5BW. Listed activities are roasting or sintering metal ore, treatment of non-hazardous waste above 50 tonnes a day, and crushing or grinding minerals. The application describes emissions, their effects on the environment and how they will be prevented, reduced and monitored. The Agency's Devon and Cornwall page says the site drew local concern under previous operators because of low-frequency noise affecting nearby communities. The Agency will decide whether to grant or refuse and what conditions to set. I did not read the application documents. Update 23 November 2026: the Environment Agency's Devon and Cornwall engagement page (read in full) says the company wants to permanently add the mobile front end (crushing, screening and washing) it has run since a Local Enforcement Position issued on 7 July 2026 to the permitted processing facility, and to extend the installation boundary to include it. The Agency says it can only refuse on technical evidence of harm that cannot be controlled, and takes health advice from the UK Health Security Agency.
items.how: Email comments to pscpublicresponse@environment-agency.gov.uk by 11 December 2026, quoting EPR/AP3203ML/V003. For help, or if you cannot email, call 03708 506 506. Comments normally go on the public register with your name; say if you do not want that.

items.title: Sale of KEVICC land in Totnes, including the Lower Field playing field
items.body: Education South West (academy trust for KEVICC, Totnes)
items.time: No consultation open. The trust says the land will be marketed from January 2027 for three months (per Totnes Pulse, 11 November 2026).
items.plain: The academy trust plans to sell three parcels of KEVICC school land in Totnes, including the Lower Field long used for sport. Campaigners are preparing a community bid to keep the field.
items.detail: From Totnes Pulse (11 November 2026, read in full) on a public meeting of about 100 people on 10 November: the Government agreed in February 2025 that three parcels could be sold (the Sheep field, the 1920s Elmhirst building and the field beside it, not the riverside field or the all-weather pitch); the local plan allocates the Elmhirst site for housing. The trust's leaders said every penny would go to KEVICC and that the asset of community value period ends on 20 November, but the land would be marketed from January for three months. Totnes Town Council's mayor said the council could not fund a purchase alone and would consult before any council tax rise for it. Friends of Lower Field (3 November) question the original 2021 consultation and the changed improvement plans. Classing the trust as a charity is my reading (academy trusts are charitable companies).
items.how: No formal consultation. Contact Friends of Lower Field, Totnes Town Council or Education South West to give your view.

petitions.title: Safely reopen Mount Batten Beach and peninsula
petitions.outcome: Presented in the House of Commons on 14 September 2026 by Rebecca Smith MP with almost 2,000 signatures, plus almost 1,700 from a similar online petition. The beach has been closed since 10 July 2026 after asbestos fibres were found in sand samples. Plymouth City Council says re-opening is a high priority but a complex task (BBC 10 October 2026, snippet). Still closed as far as I could verify.

petitions.title: Reverse the decision to move 13 South Hams parishes into Greater Plymouth (Rebecca Smith MP)
petitions.outcome: BBC Devon reported more than 4,200 signatures, presented in Parliament in early September 2026 (the BBC article of 2 September says 'being presented on Wednesday'). The Prime Minister said he would look again, and the MP reports the Government then paused and reviewed the Devon plans (see the reorganisation item). Withdrawal has been reported but not confirmed by me.

petitions.title: Petition against Devon local government reorganisation (Caroline Voaden MP)
petitions.outcome: BBC Devon reported almost 2,000 signatures, presented in Parliament the same week. About 2,000 is the BBC's wording; the exact figure is not published. See the Prime Minister's reply above.

petitions.title: Referendum on a directly elected mayor for Plymouth (Yesdemplymouth)
petitions.outcome: Campaign handed in 13,250 written signatures (The Herald, 29 January 2025); the council confirmed 10,856 valid signatures, above the 5 percent needed, so a referendum was held. ITV reported the result on 18 July 2025 (search snippet): 19,840 for the existing leader model, 18,044 for a mayor, turnout 19.1 percent. Plymouth kept its leader model.

petitions.title: Have your say! Central Park deserves better!
petitions.outcome: Council e-petition ran 16 July to 31 August 2024 and finished with 1,790 signatures (council petition page, seen in a search result). I could not open the page, so the council's response is not verified. (Council pages could not be opened on 1 November 2026 to re-confirm this.)

petitions.title: Save the Trees of Armada Way (STRAW)
petitions.outcome: Presented to Full Council on 30 January 2023. The Plymouth Herald reported about 10,000 signatures, about 5,000 from Plymouth postcodes (the group later says almost 17,000). Councillors voted 18 for, 5 against, 22 abstentions for a period of meaningful community engagement before designs were finalised. The felling went ahead overnight on 14 March 2023 until a High Court injunction saved about 20 trees (STRAW). An independent review reported by the BBC on 22 May 2025 put the cost at more than 3.3 million pounds.

petitions.title: Keep bus shelters in Efford and Lipson (Deer Park)
petitions.outcome: The Herald (20 March 2022) reported a petition with more than 200 signatures handed to the council by ward councillors; exact count not published. The council said the removal programme would start on 22 March 2022, cutting shelters from 626 to 415, and that shelters still served by a bus would be replaced by a stop. The article does not say how the petition itself was answered.

petitions.title: Devils Point Slab
petitions.outcome: Plymouth City Council e-petition. Signing ended on 4 November 2026 and the council's e-petitions list now shows it as 'Finished' with 4 respondents (read through the home-computer scrape of 9 November 2026). I did not read the petition's own page, so what it asked for and any council response are not verified.
